messages:
maria: FYI customer @jdoe started seeing a cluster of 504s after switching to our Go SDK and using a custom http.Client with per-request context cancel. They say failures spike under load. Logs attached.

sam: which SDK version and what does the http.Client look like? often this is an issue with reusing clients vs creating per-request clients.

customer-jdoe: thanks — we are on github.com/redwood/inference-go v1.2.3. minimal repro below (we run many goroutines each doing this):

```go
client := &http.Client{
    Transport: &http.Transport{
        DisableKeepAlives: true, // we set this while debugging
        MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 10,
    },
    Timeout: 5 * time.Second, // per-client timeout
}
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", body)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
if err != nil { log.Println("err", err) }
```

We see: "net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)" and server logs show repeated retries from our side and a few 502/504 spikes. Also we see many connections in TIME_WAIT.

runtime-bot: ALERT: increased 5xx rate on /v1/generate in us-west-2 (p90 latency 2.3s -> 5.8s).

andrew: thanks for the repro, @jdoe. a couple quick notes:
- don't mix http.Client.Timeout and per-request context.WithTimeout; Client.Timeout cancels the whole request including retries at the transport layer which can lead to mid-retry cancellations that look like server 5xx in metrics. prefer request context for per-call deadlines.
- setting DisableKeepAlives=true will prevent connection reuse and can cause connection churn (lots of TIME_WAIT) which increases latency under load. try reusing a single client with Transport defaults and tune IdleConnTimeout / MaxIdleConns.
- our Go SDK v1.2.3 had a conservative retry wrapper that didn't always distinguish client-cancel errors from server errors; we fixed this in v1.3.0 so the client won't retry on context cancellations. please try v1.3.1.

Suggested quick repro steps for support to validate:
1) reproduce using a pooled client (single http.Client reused) and remove DisableKeepAlives.
2) remove client.Timeout and use ctx timeouts: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 3*time.Second) per request.
3) upgrade to inference-go v1.3.1 and rerun the load.
4) capture tcp states (ss -tan) and SDK logs with TRACE=redwood:retry.

sam: can you paste the SDK config snippet they use for retries? how many attempts and backoff?

customer-jdoe: config snippet: "retries": 3, "backoff_ms": 200 (we left defaults).

andrew: 3 retries with client-side timeouts + DisableKeepAlives explains the duplicate work and metric noise. immediate mitigation: set DisableKeepAlives=false, reuse client, and deploy v1.3.1. Long term: we'll backport a check so the SDK will not attempt retries when the request context is already canceled.

maria: assigning to @andrew for eng-runtime follow-up and patch. can support share the customer's test harness and the load generator? also ask customer to run the steps above and report p50/p95 before/after. :thumbsup:

andrew: on it — I'll open an internal ticket (ENG-rt-789) and follow up here with a patch ETA. thanks for the fast triage everyone.

customer-jdoe: thanks — will try the change and report back in ~1h. appreciate the quick help. :pray:
